correctness.rationale: The Bernoulli KL normalization gives f(0)=f'(0)=0, f'(1)=1, f''>0, rho=f(1) in (0,1). The derivative of eta_h=f(y)/(y+hs), y=1-e^-s, has numerator u[y f'(y)-f(y)]-h[f(y)-su f'(y)], u=e^-s. For h small this has a unique large-s root where u~h rho/(1-rho), giving s_h=log(1/h)+log[(1-rho)/rho]+O(h log1/h) and the stated eta loss. In linear response f=y²/2, the optimizer solves h=(1-e^-s)/(e^s-1-2s) for s>s_p, and this threshold decreases strictly from infinity to zero; small/large-h expansions follow Taylor and pole inversion. A separate finite parameter calculation verified forward/reverse KL normalization rho~0.558363 and reverse/forward~0.790949 for beta=1 E=2 a=1.2. These finite checks do not prove global asymptotics.
